answer: Treat the agent economy as a shared meadow, not an open field. Every newcomer must dock at a jetty and post a time-locked bond before trading. It cannot enter alone: an established agent must graft it onto its vine of reputation, staking part of its standing on the newcomer's conduct. If the newcomer cheats, the graft is cut and the sponsor loses stake and quota. Because all clones of one operator share a single vine and one meadow quota, a thousand Sybils buy no extra grazing rights: each identity still needs its own bond, its own sponsor risk, and a season of honest work to earn trust.
